Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a concise runbook and an example export schema CSV.

1) Retention defaults:
- Audit logs (control-plane events, auth changes): 365 days default for hosted customers.
- Access logs (request-level HTTP/auth events): 180 days default.
- We offer extended retention (multi-year) as an add-on for customers on Dedicated or Private installs; policy is configurable per-tenant.

2) Export capabilities:
- Exports can be full-range or filtered by tenant_id, date range, event_type, and resource_id.
- Exports are prepared as ndjson or CSV; 1 TB/day export throughput typical for hosted tier, with per-request limits (100k events/request) to protect runtime.
- For very large exports we provide a staged export (background job) with status callbacks and a signed GCS/Azure S3 URL for download.

3) Post-export deletability:
- Export artifacts held on Redwood-managed storage are retained for 14 days by default to allow retries. Customers may request earlier deletion via the support portal; we provide a deletion confirmation once completed. For Dedicated/Private customers exports can be written to customer-controlled buckets per contract.

4) Deletion/erasement timeline:
- When retention expires, records enter a 30-day soft-delete (shadow) window during which restoration is possible by support. After 30 days we permanently purge and overwrite indexes per our purge playbook. For regulatory erasure requests we can accelerate the purge and provide an attestation.

I've attached: audit-export-runbook.pdf (runbook with steps + roles) and export_schema_v2.csv (sample manifest and field list). If you want, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with our ops team before your review.

Thanks — small clarification for Acme's procurement/legal: for Dedicated customers who commit to a reserved capacity contract, the export retention window for held artifacts (the 14-day export artifact hold) can be changed in the SOW. For Private we generally default to customer-controlled buckets and do not hold copies unless expressly enabled for operational recovery.

Also noting that size-based throttles are important: the 100k events/request is a soft limit; very large ad-hoc exports are routed to background jobs which generate a signed URL and chunked files (we shard by day/resource). Happy to provide an example background job timeline if helpful.

Thanks all — looping in a short ops checklist to make this actionable for Acme's review.

Action items for Acme compliance (we can own items 2 and 4 if you prefer):
1) Confirm the export format you prefer (ndjson vs CSV) — CSV sample attached.
2) If you want exports delivered to your cloud storage, provide a write-only presigned bucket path and we will configure S3/GCS delivery during the background job (no copies persist on our side beyond the agreed hold period).
3) Let us know if you require an extended retention add-on (we will include pricing in the SOW).
4) For erasure requests, send the legal ticket to security@redwoodinference.com with the tenant_id and timeframe; we will provide an erasure attestation.

Operational notes: automated purge is policy-driven and auditable — we log purge actions to the tamper-evident audit trail and include a deletion hash in the attestation. The soft-delete window (30 days) exists to support recovery from operational incidents; it is not searchable via the standard API.

Scheduling: Olga/Rafael — happy to run a 30-minute call with Acme on Thursday 11/25 or Friday 11/26 to walk the runbook and show a live export demo. Daniel — which slot works for you?
